examples.ko: 촬영 중에 엔지가 나서 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: A take went wrong during filming, so we shot it again.
The actor got a line wrong and caused an NG.
A video collecting only the blooper scenes is popular.

examples.ko: 이번 장면은 엔지 없이 한 번에 끝났어요.
examples.en: This scene finished in one go without any retakes.
When the director shouted NG, everyone stopped.

examples.ko: 엔지 때문에 촬영이 두 시간이나 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: Because of the retakes, filming ran two hours late.

explain: '엔지'는 영어 NG에서 온 말로, 영화나 방송 촬영에서 다시 찍어야 하는 장면을 가리켜요. '엔지가 나다', '엔지를 내다'로 자주 말해요. 방송 밖에서 일을 망쳤을 때는 '실수'나 '망치다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I laughed so much that there was a flubbed take.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장면이 잘못되어 다시 찍어야 하는 일이 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means something went wrong in a scene and it had to be filmed again.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 엔지를 거의 안 내요.
phrases.en: That actor hardly ever messes up a take.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엔지가 나다'와 달리 사람이 주어가 되어 일을 틀린 쪽에 초점이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '엔지가 나다', the person is the subject, so the focus is on who made the mistake.

phrases.example: 엔지 장면이 본 영화보다 더 재미있어요.
phrases.en: The NG scenes are more fun than the movie itself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 방송에서 틀리거나 웃다가 다시 찍은 장면을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to scenes in a film or show that were reshot because of mistakes or laughing.

explain_en: 엔지 comes from the English NG and refers to a scene that must be shot again in film or broadcast work. People say 엔지가 나다 and 엔지를 내다. Outside of broadcasting, use 실수 or 망치다 for a mistake or a ruined job.

examples.en: This song is my own composition.
My friend sang me his own song on the guitar.
I want to enter the contest with my own song.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 자작곡이 많아서 인기가 있어요.
examples.en: That singer has many self-written songs and is popular.

examples.ko: 자작곡 한 곡을 완성하는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to finish one original song.
Where can I listen to your original songs?

explain: 자기가 만든 노래는 '자작곡', 남의 노래를 다시 부른 건 '커버곡'이에요. '자작-'은 '자작시'처럼 직접 지은 것 앞에 붙고, 곡을 직접 만드는 사람은 '싱어송라이터'라고 많이 불러요.

phrases.example: 친구가 생일 선물로 자작곡을 만들어 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend made me an original song as a birthday present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 노래를 만들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means one created the song oneself.

phrases.en: I sang my own song on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 만든 노래를 노래할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when singing a song one has made oneself.

phrases.en: This is a song I made myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자작곡'을 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to explain what '자작곡' means.

explain_en: A song you made yourself is 자작곡, while a song you sing again from someone else is a 커버곡 (cover). The prefix 자작- also appears in '자작시' (a poem you wrote), and a performer who writes their own songs is often called a 싱어송라이터.

examples.en: The children made animals out of clay.
Clay gets hard when it dries.
They told us to bring clay to art class.
Clay sticks to my hands and is hard to wash off.

examples.ko: 비닐로 덮어 두면 찰흙이 마르지 않아요.
examples.en: If you cover it with plastic, the clay won't dry out.
I kneaded the clay and shaped it into a bowl.

explain: 학교 미술 시간이나 아이들 공작에서 가장 흔히 듣는 점토 이름이에요. 도자기나 공예 분야에서는 '점토'라는 말도 써요.

phrases.en: People use clay when making pottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찰흙과 같은 뜻이지만 공예나 도자기 분야에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common in crafts and pottery.

phrases.en: I played with clay with my child on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들이 찰흙으로 노는 활동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to children's play activity with clay.

phrases.en: I shaped clay by hand and made a bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찰흙을 손으로 모양 내어 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual verb pairing for shaping clay by hand.

explain_en: This is the most common name for clay in school art classes and children's crafts. In ceramics and crafts the word '점토' is also used.

examples.en: The author is publishing a new novel this fall.
This publisher only published children's books.
I want to publish my diary as a book.

examples.ko: 시집을 출판할 때 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Publishing a book of poems costs a lot of money.
To publish a paper, you have to go through review.

examples.ko: 그 책은 십 년 전에 출판했는데 아직도 팔려요.
examples.en: They published that book ten years ago, and it still sells.

explain: 책, 시집, 논문처럼 글을 책으로 만들어 세상에 내놓을 때 써요. 신문, 잡지, 카드, 영수증은 '발행하다'를 써서 구별해요.

phrases.example: 그는 어린 시절 이야기를 책으로 출판했어요.
phrases.en: He published the story of his childhood as a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 책으로 만들어 세상에 내놓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when turning writing into a book for the public.

phrases.en: That novel was published last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책이 주어일 때는 '출판되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '출판되다' when the book is the subject.

phrases.en: I sent my manuscript to a publisher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 만들어 내는 회사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The company that makes and publishes books.

explain_en: Active; to publish a book or work, by a publisher or an author (책을 출판해요) Use it for turning writing into a book and releasing it, such as novels, poetry, and papers. For newspapers, magazines, cards, and receipts, '발행하다' is the word.

gh: a book comes out; neutral, written
very formal; publish periodicals or old texts

p.n: 출간 stresses the book coming out; 출판 covers the whole publishing process.

t90.ax: I want to publish my diary as a book.

examples.en: The children are spinning tops in the yard.
This top spins for a long time, which is amazing.

examples.ko: 팽이가 쓰러지기 전에 한 번 더 쳐요.
examples.en: I hit the top once more before it falls over.

examples.ko: 시장에서 색깔이 예쁜 팽이 하나를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a top with pretty colors at the market.
I spun around like a top and sat down because I felt dizzy.

examples.ko: 얼음 위에서 팽이를 치는 놀이가 재미있어요.
examples.en: Playing with tops on the ice is fun.

explain: 줄을 감아 던져 돌리는 팽이는 '돌리다', 채로 쳐서 오래 돌게 하는 팽이는 '치다'를 같이 써요. 겨울에 얼음 위에서 하는 '팽이치기'는 한국 전통 놀이예요. '팽이버섯'의 이름에도 들어가요.

phrases.en: The child spins a top on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄을 감아 던져서 돌리는 팽이에 써요. 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for tops spun by winding a string and throwing. The most basic phrase.

phrases.en: In winter, we play top-whipping on the ice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전통 놀이 이름이에요. '하다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a traditional game. Used with 하다.

phrases.en: If you hit the top with a stick, it spins for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채로 때려서 계속 돌게 할 때 써요. '돌리다'와 쓰임이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you keep a top spinning by hitting it with a stick. Different from 돌리다.

explain_en: A top you wind with a string and throw goes with '돌리다', and a top you keep spinning by hitting it with a stick goes with '치다'. '팽이치기' on winter ice is a traditional Korean game. The word is also part of '팽이버섯' (enoki mushroom).

examples.ko: 바다 위에서 갈매기가 시끄럽게 울고 있어요.
examples.en: A seagull is crying loudly over the sea.

examples.ko: 배를 타면 갈매기에게 과자를 던져 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a boat, you can throw snacks to the seagulls.
The seagull cheering song at the Busan baseball stadium is famous.
White seagulls are flying around the beach.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 갈매기를 처음 봤을 때 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: When I first saw a seagull as a kid, I was startled.
Seagulls live by catching and eating fish.

explain: 바닷가 이야기에 자주 나오는 새예요. '갈매기가 날다', '갈매기가 울다'처럼 말해요. '갈매기살'은 이름만 같고 새가 아니라 돼지고기의 한 부위니까 메뉴판에서 놀라지 마세요.

phrases.en: Seagulls are flying in the sky over the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다 풍경을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase when describing a seaside scene.

phrases.example: 아침에 갈매기가 우는 소리에 잠이 깼어요.
phrases.en: I woke up to the sound of seagulls crying in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 소리를 낸다는 뜻이에요. 새가 '울다'라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the bird makes its call; Korean says a bird 'cries' (울다).

phrases.en: A flock of seagulls followed behind the boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갈매기가 여러 마리 모인 모습을 말해요. '떼'는 무리라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A group of many seagulls; 떼 means flock.

explain_en: This is a bird that often appears in stories about the seaside. Koreans say '갈매기가 날다' or '갈매기가 울다'. '갈매기살' only shares the name; it is not the bird but a cut of pork, so don't be surprised when you see it on a menu.

examples.en: My grandfather spread manure on the field.
I'm collecting fallen leaves to use as fertilizer.
The vegetables grow well because the soil is well fertilized.

examples.ko: 음식물 쓰레기를 거름으로 만드는 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to turn food waste into compost.
I closed the window because of the smell of manure.

examples.ko: 거름을 너무 많이 주면 식물이 죽을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you give too much fertilizer, the plant can die.

explain: 거름은 똥이나 낙엽처럼 자연에서 얻은 재료를 말하는 때가 많고, 공장에서 만든 것은 '비료'라고 해요. 도시에서는 '비료'가 더 흔해요. '걸음'(걷는 것)과 소리가 같아서 글자로 구별해야 해요.

phrases.en: I give fertilizer to the trees in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물에 거름을 넣어 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for putting fertilizer on plants.

phrases.en: I spread factory-made fertilizer on the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거름'은 자연 재료, '비료'는 공장에서 만든 것에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '거름' is natural material; '비료' is closer to factory-made.

phrases.en: Even failure becomes good fertilizer later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 도움이 되는 경험이라는 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively for an experience that helps later.

explain_en: 거름 often refers to natural material such as dung or leaves, while factory-made products are called '비료'. In cities '비료' is more common. It sounds the same as '걸음' (a step), so tell them apart by spelling.

examples.en: On autumn nights you can hear crickets.
A cricket came into the room.
The kids searched the grass to catch a cricket.
Crickets make sound by rubbing their wings.
When I hear a cricket's chirp, I feel autumn.
I first saw a cricket at my grandmother's country house.

explain: 귀뚜라미 소리는 한국에서 가을을 알리는 소리로 자주 써요. 소리는 '귀뚤귀뚤'이라고 표현해요. 여름 매미와 짝으로 '매미는 여름, 귀뚜라미는 가을'이라고 느끼는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: I can hear the crickets loudly at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을밤의 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to evoke an autumn night.

phrases.en: A chirping sound comes from outside the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀뚜라미 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word that imitates a cricket's chirp.

phrases.en: When autumn came, the crickets started chirping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귀뚜라미의 소리를 말할 때는 '울다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 울다 for a cricket's call.

explain_en: In Korea, cricket sounds often signal autumn. The sound is written as 귀뚤귀뚤. Many people pair it with the summer cicada: 매미 for summer, 귀뚜라미 for fall.

en: floral scent; fragrance of a flower

examples.en: When I opened the window, the first thing I noticed was the scent of flowers.
Smelling flower fragrance makes me feel good.
The scent of flowers also comes carried on the spring breeze.
This scented candle has a gentle floral scent, which I like.
I was lost in the flower fragrance and stood there for a long time.

examples.ko: 꽃향기 때문에 재채기가 나는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people sneeze because of the scent of flowers.

explain: '냄새'보다 기분 좋은 느낌의 '향기'를 쓴 말이에요. '꽃향기를 맡다'처럼 '맡다'와 같이 써요. 가볍게는 '꽃냄새'라고도 하지만 좋은 향을 말할 때는 '꽃향기'가 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: A floral scent comes from the garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃향기'에 '나다'를 붙여 향이 느껴진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 나다 to 꽃향기 says that you can smell a floral scent.

phrases.en: In spring, the park is full of the scent of flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 향이 아주 많이 퍼져 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the scent is spread everywhere.

phrases.en: After the rain, it smells like flowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃향기'보다 가볍고 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, more casual word than 꽃향기.

explain_en: It uses '향기' (fragrance) rather than '냄새' (smell), so it has a pleasant feel. It pairs with '맡다', as in '꽃향기를 맡다'. People casually say '꽃냄새' too, but '꽃향기' suits a nice scent better.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나 보니 나팔꽃이 활짝 피었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, the morning glories were in full bloom.
The child planted morning glory seeds in a pot.

examples.ko: 나팔꽃은 해가 뜨면 피고 오후에는 시들어요.
examples.en: Morning glories open when the sun rises and wilt in the afternoon.
Morning glory vines climb along the fence.
The morning glory is purple and so pretty.
I observed morning glories for my summer vacation homework.

explain: 꽃 모양이 나팔 같아서 붙은 이름이에요. 초등학교 여름방학 관찰 숙제에 자주 나오는 꽃이에요.

phrases.en: Morning glories bloom on summer mornings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피는 모습을 말하는 가장 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pairing for a flower blooming.

phrases.en: By midday the morning glories had wilted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나팔꽃은 낮에 시드는 특징이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Morning glories are known to wilt around midday.

phrases.en: There are many purple morning glories on the fence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔을 앞에 붙여 꽃을 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a color in front to describe the flower.

explain_en: The name comes from the flower's trumpet-like shape. It is a flower that often appears in elementary school summer observation homework.

examples.en: Snow blossoms covered the winter mountain.

examples.ko: 주말에 눈꽃을 보러 태백산에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This weekend I am going to Taebaeksan to see the snow-covered trees.
Snow blossoms sparkle in the sunlight.
A snow blossom festival is being held, so there are many people.
She wore a dress as white as snow blossoms.

examples.ko: 눈꽃과 함께 찍은 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The photo taken with the snow blossoms is really pretty.

explain: '눈꽃이 피다'처럼 눈이 나뭇가지에 하얗게 쌓인 모습을 꽃에 빗대어 말해요. 하늘에서 내리는 눈 한 알 한 알은 '눈송이'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I went to a snow blossom festival in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈꽃을 보는 겨울 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A winter event for seeing snow blossoms.

phrases.en: This year I want to go on a snow blossom trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 쌓인 산이나 나무를 보러 가는 여행이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A trip to see snowy mountains or trees.

phrases.en: I went to see the snow blossoms with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구경'은 재미있게 보는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '구경' means looking at something for enjoyment.

explain_en: '눈꽃이 피다' compares snow piled white on branches to flowers in bloom. Each flake falling from the sky is a '눈송이'.

examples.en: On the southern coast, camellias bloom in winter.

examples.ko: 눈 위에 빨간 동백 꽃송이가 툭 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: A red camellia blossom dropped onto the snow.
I hear there was a time when people styled their hair with camellia oil.

examples.ko: 동백은 겨울에도 잎이 푸르러서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: Camellias stand out because their leaves stay green even in winter.

examples.ko: 동백 숲길을 걸으며 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took lots of photos while walking along the camellia forest path.

examples.ko: 엄마는 동백 그림이 있는 접시를 좋아하세요.
examples.en: Mom likes plates with a camellia painting.

explain: 동백은 겨울에서 봄 사이, 특히 제주도와 남쪽 바닷가에서 피는 붉은 꽃이에요. 꽃이 질 때 송이째 툭 떨어지는 모습이 특징이라 노래와 시에 자주 나와요. 나무와 꽃을 모두 동백이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: When spring came, the camellia flowers bloomed fully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃만 가리킬 때는 '동백꽃'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you mean the flower itself.

phrases.example: 집 앞에 동백나무를 한 그루 심었어요.
phrases.en: I planted a camellia tree in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 가리킬 때는 '동백나무'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you mean the tree.

phrases.en: In Jeju, camellias bloom even in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피는 모습을 말할 때 '피다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 'to bloom' when describing the flowers opening.

explain_en: 동백 is a red flower that blooms between winter and spring, especially on 제주도 and the southern coast. It drops whole blossoms at once when it fades, which is why it often appears in songs and poems. Both the tree and the flower are called 동백.

t90.ax: Mom likes plates with a camellia painting.

examples.ko: 정원에 두더지가 땅을 파서 구멍이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A mole dug in the garden and left holes.
Moles live underground, so their eyes are small.
I played the whack-a-mole game at the arcade.

examples.ko: 아이는 책에서 본 두더지가 귀엽다고 했어요.
examples.en: The child said the mole in the book was cute.
Farmers are worried because there are many moles in the fields.
It's a day when I want to hide underground like a mole.

explain: '두더지'는 땅속에 굴을 파고 사는 작은 동물이에요. 한국에서는 오락실의 '두더지 잡기' 게임으로 아이들에게도 친숙해요. 밭을 파헤치기도 해서 농사짓는 사람들은 골치 아파해요.

phrases.en: I played whack-a-mole with my friend at the arcade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오락실 게임 이름이에요. 동물보다 게임 이야기에서 많이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of an arcade game. You hear it more in talk about the game than the animal.

phrases.en: Many mole tunnels have appeared in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두더지가 땅속에 판 길을 말해요. 밭이나 정원 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The tunnels moles dig underground. Used when talking about fields or gardens.

phrases.en: I saw a mole in the garden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물은 '마리'로 세요. 숫자와 함께 쓰는 법을 익혀 두세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Animals are counted with 마리. Learn how to use it with numbers.

explain_en: 두더지 is a small animal that digs tunnels and lives underground. Children in Korea know it well through the arcade game 두더지 잡기. It also digs up fields, which gives farmers a headache.

en: occasionally; once in a while; sparsely

examples.ko: 비가 그치고 하늘에 별이 드문드문 보였어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, a few stars could be seen here and there in the sky.

examples.ko: 그 길에는 가로등이 드문드문 서 있어요.
examples.en: Streetlights stand sparsely along that road.

examples.ko: 저는 일기를 드문드문 써서 빠진 날이 많아요.
examples.en: I write my diary only now and then, so many days are missing.

examples.ko: 시골 마을이라 집이 드문드문 흩어져 있어요.
examples.en: It's a country village, so the houses are scattered far apart.
I hear from that friend only once in a while.

examples.ko: 밤늦은 지하철에는 승객이 드문드문 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: Late at night, passengers sit sparsely on the subway.

explain: 공간에서는 사이가 멀리 떨어져 있는 모양, 시간에서는 간격이 길게 이어지는 모양에 써요. 반대로 '빽빽이', '촘촘히'는 사이가 가까운 모양이에요. '가끔'은 시간에만 쓰고, '드문드문'은 장소와 시간 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Because of the rain, customers come only here and there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 한꺼번에 오지 않고 간격을 두고 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people come at intervals rather than all at once.

phrases.en: On the mountain path, people were seen here and there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소에서 사이가 떨어져 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means things appear spread out in a place.

phrases.en: These days I only keep in touch with my friend now and then.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연락하는 간격이 길 때 써요. '가끔'과 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the gaps between contacts are long; close to 가끔.
phrases.en_equiv: keep in touch now and then

explain_en: With gaps in space or time, e.g., streetlights spread out (이 길에는 가로등이 드문드문 서 있어서 밤에 어두워요.) In space it means things are spread far apart, and in time it means events happen with long gaps. The opposites are '빽빽이' and '촘촘히' (densely). '가끔' works only for time, while '드문드문' works for both place and time.

t90.ax: Streetlights stand sparsely along that road.

examples.en: I met a wild dog on the mountain path and was startled.

examples.ko: 들개는 무리를 지어 다니는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wild dogs often move around in packs.
An abandoned dog sometimes becomes a stray.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 들개 때문에 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: The villagers are very worried about the wild dogs.

examples.ko: 들개를 보면 가까이 가지 말고 피하세요.
examples.en: If you see a wild dog, avoid it and don't go near.

examples.ko: 다큐멘터리에서 아프리카 들개가 사냥하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw African wild dogs hunting in a documentary.

explain: '들개'는 주인 없이 들이나 산에서 사는 개예요. 버려져서 떠도는 개는 '유기견'이라고 해요. '들'은 야생의 뜻을 더해서 '들고양이', '들꽃'처럼 쓰여요.

phrases.en: A pack of wild dogs came down the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들개는 여럿이 다니는 일이 많아서 '무리'와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Wild dogs often travel in groups, so it pairs with 무리 (pack).

phrases.en: A wild dog showed up at night and I was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 나타났을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when one suddenly appears.

phrases.en: Be careful of wild dogs when you go to the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving a warning.

explain_en: '들개' is a dog with no owner that lives in fields or mountains. A dog that was abandoned and wanders is called a '유기견'. The prefix '들' adds a wild feel, as in '들고양이' and '들꽃'.
